title: Firebase Firestore Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Firebase Firestore course.

entries.name: Meet collections and documents
entries.summary: A collection groups documents. Each document has an id and named fields, such as a book title and page count.

entries.name: Start a local emulator
entries.summary: An emulator imitates the service on your own computer.

example.code:
npx firebase-tools init emulators
npx firebase-tools emulators:start --only firestore --project demo-reading-club

entries.name: Write a named document
entries.summary: setDoc writes fields at a document path you choose.

entries.name: Read one document
entries.summary: getDoc reads a document snapshot. Check exists before reading fields, because the requested document may not be there.

entries.name: Let Firestore choose an id
entries.summary: addDoc adds a document to a collection with an automatically made id.

entries.name: Change selected fields
entries.summary: updateDoc changes named fields while leaving other fields alone.

entries.name: Ask for matching documents
entries.summary: A query applies a rule to a collection. getDocs returns snapshots for documents that match that rule.

entries.name: Sort and limit a query
entries.summary: orderBy sorts query results by a field. limit caps how many documents are returned.

entries.name: Listen for local updates
entries.summary: onSnapshot sends the current result and later changes.

entries.name: Group writes in a batch
entries.summary: A write batch applies several writes together.

entries.name: Keep local practice rules narrow
entries.summary: Security rules decide which client reads and writes are allowed.

entries.name: Treat stored data as input
entries.summary: A database record can have a shape your UI does not expect.
